definition: mlxtend (machine learning extensions) adds helpers to scikit-learn: stacking ensembles, feature selection, association rules and plotting.
details: Created and maintained by Sebastian Raschka since 2014.

explainer.lead: How to install mlxtend, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

quickstart.python:
from mlxtend.classifier import StackingClassifier
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsClassifier
from sklearn.naive_bayes import GaussianNB
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris

X, y = load_iris(return_X_y=True)
stack = StackingClassifier(classifiers=[KNeighborsClassifier(), GaussianNB()],
                           meta_classifier=LogisticRegression())
print(stack.fit(X, y).score(X, y))

explainer.inAi: Quick ensembles and feature-selection experiments on top of scikit-learn models.
explainer.jsNote: mlxtend is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.

tiers.eli5: It's an add-on box of extra tools for a popular machine learning toolkit, covering things the original didn't include.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers reach for it when they need stacking ensembles, feature selection, association rules or plotting alongside scikit-learn. A pitfall is dependency: it is an extension layer, so its helpers only make sense inside a scikit-learn workflow.
tiers.paperLevel: A set of machine learning extensions adding stacking ensembles, feature selection, association rules and plotting to scikit-learn. Created and maintained by Sebastian Raschka since 2014.

explainer.example: A data scientist builds a stacking ensemble and plots the results using mlxtend's helpers on top of scikit-learn.
